summary: A list of what an agent knows: uploaded files, websites it crawls and connected folders of docs, each with how far it has been indexed. A source is queued, indexing with a progress bar and a count, ready with when it last synced, or failed with the reason. A failed source can offer a fix, like reading a scanned PDF with OCR, and every source has Re-sync and Remove. It answers the question "what does this agent know, and is it up to date?"
use: When people give an agent its own knowledge, like help docs, a product site or a shared drive, and need to see what it has read.
When indexing takes a while and people should see it progress instead of waiting on a blank list.
When a source can fail for a reason people can act on, like a scanned PDF or a site that blocks crawlers.
In an agent's settings, next to its tools and memory.
features: Each source in `sources` shows its type's icon (`kind` of `files`, `web` or `folder`), its `name`, and a line under it that follows its `state`.
The dot on the icon is the state at a glance: grey while `queued`, a turning ring while `indexing`, green when `ready` and red when `failed`.
While indexing, the line becomes a progress bar and a count, like "64 of 142 pages", from `done` and `count`; `unit` switches pages to files.
A ready source reads like "142 pages · Synced 2m ago" from its `synced`; a queued one reads "Queued", or your own `note`.
A failed source shows its `error` in red, with a button labelled with its `fix` that calls `onFix`, and a Remove button when you pass `onRemove`.
Each row has a menu with Re-sync (`onResync`, unavailable while the source waits or indexes) and Remove (`onRemove`).

Add source opens a menu with an option for each handler you pass: Upload files opens the file picker and calls `onUpload` with the files; Add a website asks for an address and calls `onAddWebsite` with it, without http(s)://; Connect a folder lists `folders` and calls `onConnectFolder`.
The line under the title counts the sources and adds up their `chunks`, like "4 sources · 1,204 chunks", or shows your own `status`.
a11y: The sources form a list, and each row's menu button is named for its source, like "Actions for Product docs".
An indexing source's bar is a progressbar with its count as its value.
The menus have role="menu"; their buttons expose aria-expanded and aria-haspopup, and Escape closes a menu; in React, focus goes back to its button.
The line under the title is announced politely when it changes.
With reduced motion, rows appear without their entrance and text changes without the crossfade.

faq.a: No. It shows what you tell it. Run the indexing in your own code and update each source's `state` and `done` as it goes; the bar and count follow.

faq.q: How do I show the website being added?
faq.a: Handle `onAddWebsite`: add a source with `kind: 'web'` and `state: 'queued'`, then move it to `indexing` and `ready` as your crawler works. Pass `address` and `onAddressChange` if you want to fill in the field yourself.

faq.q: Why doesn't the chunk count include a source that is still indexing?
faq.a: The total adds up `chunks`, so leave a source's `chunks` out until it has been indexed. Keep it while a source re-syncs if its old index still answers questions.

faq.q: Can a failed source offer something other than OCR?
faq.a: Yes. `fix` is any label, like "Sign in again" or "Try a smaller file", and `onFix` gets the source's key.
